result.headline: Throttle command dropped to zero at ~117.2 s; motor channel ch[2] held 1100 us, aircraft lost airspeed and altitude.
result.explanation: The propulsion loop (throttle command and output ch[2]) went to zero and stayed there, with no mode change or event in the recording. Pitch tracking, airspeed and altitude degraded afterwards. Who or what commanded zero is not in the data.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a9 t=117.791 s: actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 to the end (see line 25; strength 4.015)
evidence.shows: The propulsion output froze at its minimum 1100 us for the last 15 s of the recording.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.971 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch[2] is the throttle/propulsion channel. The throttle command left its baseline (48 -> 0 %) at 117.193 s, before ch[2] stepped to 1100 us at 117.449 s, so the zero came from upstream of the output.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[2]] at t=117.449 s: 1476 -> 1100 us (step -376, 47x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: An abrupt step, not a gradual decline.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.airspeed changed level for good at t=121.789 s: median 15.932 before, 11.985 after m/s (5x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Airspeed fell after the throttle cut.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a11 t=120.823 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] worse for good (typical |error| 1.109 -> 4.024) (see line 77; strength 2.197)
evidence.shows: Pitch tracking error rose about 4.7x after the cut (0.657 -> 3.064 deg in compare). This is an effect.

checked.check: Sequence of who left baseline first in 110-125 s
checked.result: ch[2] drifted from 111.2 s; throttle left baseline at 117.193 s; airspeed 119.4 s; pitch 119.6 s; ch[1] 120.1 s; altitude 120.3 s. Throttle command precedes the output freeze.
ch[2] and throttle froze at 1100 us / 0 % (spread 0). Airspeed, altitude and pitch tracking degraded. Yaw tracking did not worsen (ratio 0.76).
checked.about: Propulsion loop is the first fault; the other changes are consequences

checked.result: Only two start-up messages at t=0.933 s (Battery low voltage, Sensor health). No mode change, failsafe or other event later in the recording.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.airspeed changed level for good at t=121.789 s: median 15.932 before, 11.985 after m/s (5x its variation before)
effects.why: Loss of thrust slows the aircraft.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=121.577 s: median 49.98 before, 39.075 after m (10x its variation before)
SHIFT actuator.output[ch[1]] changed level for good at t=120.56 s: median 1527 before, 1431 after us (6.9x its variation before)
effects.why: The pitch-loop channel responded after airspeed and pitch had already moved, so it compensates rather than leads.

next_action.action: Pull the flight controller's onboard log for 110-125 s and read the throttle command source.
next_action.why: Separates a commanded zero (mode, operator, failsafe) from a fault in the throttle path or power system, which this recording cannot do.
how: Read flight mode, RC throttle input and any failsafe or arming flags between 115 and 119 s
Read battery voltage and current across the same window
Check whether the zero came from autopilot output, RC, or the output mixer
next_action.conditions: Same flight, UAV-11 onboard log, 110-125 s. No flight needed.
next_action.baseline: The same signals earlier in this flight (10-110 s), where throttle held about 44-48 %.

outcomes.label: Commanded zero by mode, RC or failsafe
outcomes.means: The fault is in the command source, and the output and motor behaved as designed.
outcomes.then: Trace why that command was issued.

outcomes.label: Autopilot demanded throttle but output was 0
outcomes.means: The fault is in the mixer, the output stage or the link to the ESC.
outcomes.then: Bench test the output channel and ESC.

outcomes.label: Battery voltage sagged before 117 s
outcomes.means: A power or battery cutoff led to the throttle zero.
outcomes.then: Review the battery discharge and cutoff settings.

Why ch[2] fell from 1484 to 1380 us at 111.2 s, before the throttle command moved.

already_answered.question: When did the control fault occur?
already_answered.answer: Throttle left baseline at 117.193 s. The output stepped to 1100 us at 117.449 s and held from 117.791 s.

already_answered.question: Where on the aircraft was it?
already_answered.answer: The propulsion/throttle loop, output channel ch[2]. The pitch channel ch[1] and the other channels carried on moving.

data_requests.what: Onboard flight log with mode, RC input, battery and failsafe flags
data_requests.why_needed: Shows what commanded throttle to zero, which this recording does not contain.

unobservable.fact: Motor, ESC and wiring condition on ch[2]
unobservable.why_it_matters: A real motor or ESC fault gives the same commanded-zero picture only if the command was not zero upstream.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-test the ESC and motor with a propeller-off throttle sweep and inspect the connectors.

hypotheses.claim: Throttle was commanded to zero (mode, operator or failsafe logic) and the output followed.
hypotheses.because: Throttle command left baseline at 117.193 s, before the ch[2] output step at 117.449 s, with no event recorded.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller throttle command and output recording

hypotheses.claim: Throttle was demanded but the output channel or ESC stopped delivering it.
hypotheses.because: Output sits at the 1100 us minimum, matching the zero command. The data cannot separate a hardware fault from a commanded zero.
hypotheses.observed_at: controller output command, not the ESC

hypotheses.claim: Low battery or a power cutoff forced throttle to zero.
hypotheses.because: There is a start-up low-voltage warning at 0.933 s, but no voltage series and no later event.

hypotheses.claim: A pitch actuator or aerodynamic fault caused the pitch, airspeed and altitude changes.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed, pitch and ch[1] left baseline after the throttle command (119.4 s, 119.6 s and 120.1 s against 117.2 s), so they look like consequences.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor fault produced the apparent throttle and tracking changes.
hypotheses.because: The throttle command and the output both froze together, and several independent signals move after it. The start-up sensor-health error was not followed by anything later.

events.what: ch[2] stepped to 1100 us and held to end
events.why: Propulsion output froze after the throttle command dropped to 0.
Start-up warnings at 0.933 s; nothing later points back to them.

events.what: Airspeed, altitude and pitch tracking worsened after 119 s
events.why: These left baseline after the throttle command.
